notes.title: Sales Playbook
notes.content:
TechFlow Sales Playbook — v1.0

Target Profile:
- Companies: 50-500 employees (sweet spot)
- Industries: Tech, finance, consulting, media
- Buyer: VP Engineering, Head of Product, CTO, IT Director
- Budget: $25K-$200K annual

Sales Process:
1. Discovery (1-2 calls)
   - Understand tool stack, pain points, team size
   - Identify champion and economic buyer
   - Qualify: budget, authority, need, timeline (BANT)

2. Demo (1 call, 45 min)
   - Show cross-tool search with THEIR tools
   - AI summarization live demo
   - Context panel walkthrough
   - End with: 'Imagine this for your whole team'

3. Evaluation (1-2 weeks)
   - Pilot for champion's team (5-10 users)
   - Omar sets up onboarding
   - Weekly check-in during pilot

4. Proposal (1 call)
   - Present pricing based on team size
   - Show ROI: time saved × hourly rate × team size
   - Handle objections (see objection guide)

5. Close
   - Send contract (Elena's template)
   - Negotiate terms (net-30, annual billing)
   - Sign via DocuSign
   - Handoff to Omar for onboarding

Key differentiators to emphasize:
- Privacy-first (on-device processing)
- Speed (<200ms response time)
- Enterprise-ready (SOC2, SSO, admin controls)
- Cross-tool (not locked into one ecosystem)

notes.title: Demo Script — Enterprise
notes.content:
Enterprise Demo Script — 45 minutes

Opening (5 min):
- 'Today I'll show you how TechFlow can save your team 2 hours per person per day'
- Quick overview: what TechFlow does in 30 seconds
- Agenda: 3 live demos + Q&A

Demo 1: Cross-Tool Search (10 min)
- 'Let me search for a decision we made about X last month'
- Show: results from Slack, Notion, Google Docs simultaneously
- Highlight: speed (<1 second), relevance ranking, source attribution
- 'No more asking teammates: where did we put that document?'

Demo 2: AI Context Panel (10 min)
- 'I'm working on a project. Watch what TechFlow surfaces automatically'
- Show: relevant documents, messages, tasks appearing in sidebar
- Highlight: no query needed, proactive intelligence
- 'It's like having an assistant who always knows what you need'

Demo 3: Meeting Intelligence (10 min)
- 'I have a meeting in 5 minutes. Let me prepare'
- Show: meeting brief with attendee context, last interactions, action items
- Highlight: one-click summary after meeting
- 'Never go into a meeting unprepared again'

Enterprise Features (5 min):
- Admin dashboard (show screenshots — not live yet)
- SSO configuration
- SOC2 compliance badge
- Audit log sample

Close (5 min):
- ROI calculation: 2 hours/day × $75/hr × 200 employees = $7.5M/year saved
- Pricing overview (high-level)
- Next steps: pilot for their team
- Q&A

notes.title: Objection Handling Guide
notes.content:
Common Objections & Responses

1. 'We already use Notion AI / Slack AI'
→ 'Those tools only work within their own silo. TechFlow connects all your tools into one intelligent layer. When you search in Notion AI, you won't find your Slack messages or GitHub PRs.'

2. 'We're worried about data security'
→ 'We're SOC2 Type I certified. Free tier processes everything on-device. Enterprise tier adds SSO, admin controls, audit logs, and optional data residency. Happy to connect you with our security team.'

3. 'It's too expensive'
→ 'Let's calculate the ROI. If each team member saves just 1 hour/week (and our users report 2+ hours/day), at a $75/hr blended rate, for a team of 100, that's $390K/year in recovered productivity. Our cost? $50K.'

4. 'We need to evaluate other options'
→ 'Absolutely, who else are you looking at? [If Glean]: Great product, but 10x our price. [If Notion AI]: Limited to Notion only. We'd love to pilot alongside their evaluation — no commitment.'

5. 'We need HIPAA compliance' (healthcare)
→ 'We're working toward HIPAA compliance for Q4 2026. Happy to discuss a future commitment with a signed BAA for when we're ready.'

6. 'Can we get a longer trial?'
→ 'Standard pilot is 2 weeks for up to 10 users. For enterprise evaluations, we can extend to 30 days with CSM support. Let me set that up.'

7. 'What if you shut down?' (startup risk)
→ 'We're backed by Sequoia, have 18 months of runway, and growing rapidly. We also offer data export at any time — you're never locked in.'

notes.title: Enterprise Deal Negotiation Notes
notes.content:
Enterprise Deal Negotiation — Key Learnings

From Acme Corp process:

What worked:
- Leading with ROI calculation (2 hours saved × team size × hourly rate)
- Having Tina on the demo call (product credibility)
- Being transparent about SOC2 timeline (built trust)
- Sharing our product roadmap (showed commitment)

What to improve:
- Should have identified security blocker earlier (Sarah Chen)
- Need SOC2 report ready BEFORE engaging enterprise prospects
- Dave Kumar (CFO) should have been in first meeting
- Contract negotiation is slow — start earlier

Negotiation tactics that worked:
- Anchoring at full price, then offering 2-year discount
- Framing as 'investment in productivity' not 'software expense'
- Reference other customers of similar size
- Offering pilot with easy off-ramp (reduces perceived risk)

Deal structure patterns:
- Annual prepay → standard pricing
- Quarterly billing → 10% premium
- Multi-year → 15-25% discount
- Include implementation in first-year fee (vs charging separately)

Note to self: For next enterprise deal, get legal team (Elena) involved earlier. Contract redlines added 2 weeks to Acme process.

notes.title: CRM Pipeline Management Notes
notes.content:
CRM & Pipeline Management — Process Notes

Tool: HubSpot (free tier, upgrading to Starter in Q2)

Deal stages:
1. Lead (new inbound or outbound contact)
2. Qualified (BANT confirmed)
3. Discovery (first call completed)
4. Demo (product demo delivered)
5. Proposal (pricing sent)
6. Negotiation (terms discussion)
7. Closed Won / Closed Lost

Rules:
- Update deal stage within 24 hours of change

Reporting:
- Weekly pipeline review (every Monday)
- Monthly forecast to Sarah
- Quarterly board metrics

Metrics I track:
- Pipeline coverage ratio (target: 3x quota)
- Win rate by stage
- Average deal size (trending up)
- Sales cycle length by segment
- Lead response time (<2 hours target)

Upgrade plan (Q2):
- HubSpot Starter ($45/month) for sequences and reporting
- Eventually need Sales Hub Professional when we hire AEs ($500/month)
- ROI of upgrade: if it helps close 1 extra deal/month, pays for itself 100x

notes.title: Competitive Intelligence — Glean
notes.content:
Competitive Intelligence: Glean
Last updated: 2026-02-20

Overview:
- Enterprise AI search platform
- Series C ($200M raised, $2.2B valuation)
- 500+ enterprise customers
- Pricing: $50-60/user/month (enterprise only)

Strengths:
- Massive integration library (100+ connectors)
- Strong enterprise credibility (Fortune 500 customers)
- Dedicated support team
- Proven at scale (10K+ seat deployments)

Weaknesses:
- Very expensive (10x our price)
- Slow deployment (weeks to months)
- No SMB/mid-market play (min deal size ~$100K)
- Less innovative UX (search-first, no proactive context)
- Privacy concerns (all data in their cloud)

How we win against Glean:
1. PRICE: '$50/seat/year vs $50/seat/month — 12x cheaper'
2. SPEED: 'Deploy in 5 minutes, not 5 weeks'
3. PRIVACY: 'On-device processing option — they can't match this'
4. UX: 'Proactive intelligence, not just reactive search'

When we lose to Glean:
- Company already has Glean contract (switching cost)
- Company needs 100+ integrations (we have 6 today)
- Company needs proven scale (we're new)

Intel from deals:
- Acme Corp got Glean quote: $120K/year for 200 seats
- MetaServe chose Glean (existing relationship, couldn't justify switch)
- Zenith Labs: 'We looked at Glean but it's overkill for our size'

notes.title: Sales Forecasting Model
notes.content:
Sales Forecasting Methodology

Approach: Weighted pipeline by stage + historical conversion rates

Stage conversion rates (from Q1 data):
- Lead → Qualified: 60%
- Qualified → Discovery: 80%
- Discovery → Demo: 85%
- Demo → Proposal: 70%
- Proposal → Negotiation: 85%
- Negotiation → Closed Won: 90%

Overall funnel conversion (Lead → Closed): ~25%

Weighted pipeline calculation:
- Discovery deals: ACV × 20%
- Demo deals: ACV × 40%
- Proposal deals: ACV × 60%
- Negotiation deals: ACV × 90%

Monthly forecast template:
- Committed (90%+): deals in Negotiation stage
- Likely (60-89%): deals at Proposal stage
- Pipeline (20-59%): deals at Demo or Discovery
- Upside (<20%): new leads or stalled deals

Accuracy tracking:
- January forecast: $50K predicted, $51K actual (98% accuracy)
- February forecast: $70K predicted, $64K actual (91% accuracy)
- March forecast: $100K committed + $35K likely = $135K predicted

Goal: Maintain >85% forecast accuracy for board reporting.
